about: PRAX, Catalyst Event PM, Mon 2026-11-16. The thesis as the 08:02 morning run (cmwj9vxkz000k08lbwd64wbh7) left it, and the two trigger runs' update_thesis calls verbatim from RunMessage (role thread).

triggers.rationale: A close above the 20-session high of $351.64 confirms the pre-PDUFA run-up has started — that is the signal I need before entering. Send to me; I want to confirm nothing changed on the regulatory front before buying.
Flag for review two weeks before the December 27 PDUFA date — this is when I'd plan to exit the position if we are in it, to avoid holding through the binary.
Any material agreement 8-K filed by Praxis could signal a partnership or licensing deal that changes the commercial picture — send to me same day.

A close below $236 would mean the market has decided the regulatory path is broken — if relutrigine's review produces a refuse-to-file or a clinical hold, that is what this level reflects. The structure under it is the October 14 swing low of $236.79; the stop sits just under that level, which is 1.3× ATR(14) of $18.25 below the swing low. Because this is a binary event setup, size is the actual risk control — a gap will skip any stop, and the $236 level is structural and advisory, not a hard exit on a gap down.

A review at the August 20 high of $392.70 — the prior peak before the PDUFA extension drove the selloff. If the stock reaches that level before December 10, I'll trim and reassess; the real exit rule is a sale 1–2 weeks before the December 27 decision date regardless of price, to avoid holding through the binary.
A new 8-K press release from Praxis could carry an FDA update, trial news, or launch change ahead of the Dec. 27 decision, so send it to me the same day.
A new 8-K other-events filing from Praxis could disclose a regulatory or commercial development that changes the pre-decision setup, so send it to me the same day.

input.rationale: Praxis is down about 2% this morning, and I’m holding the watch with the buy plan unchanged. I corrected the filing wake issue by keeping the same-day 7.01 and 8.01 reviews in place, and I would only change the call on a close above $351.75 or on a real FDA problem or cheap stock sale before year-end.
